proof.criterion: Round 2 finding 4: the case-insensitive pull-request reads are bounded by an index again, as migration 0062 decided they should be.
proof.surface: PostgreSQL's own planner, on a scratch database of the daemon's migrations with 20 000 pull requests over 40 repositories, ANALYZEd, with the three queries exactly as store.go spells them
proof.command: EXPLAIN on PullRequestByBranch, PullRequestByNumber and PullRequestRecorded, before and after the new migration
proof.observed: Before, each read was an Index Scan whose only Index Cond was the branch or the number, with lower(repo) as a Filter; after, both columns are Index Conds, on pull_requests_lower_repo_branch and pull_requests_lower_repo_number. One correction to the finding, which the new comment carries: on PostgreSQL 18 these reads did not scan the table — the surviving condition kept them in the index — but they walked the whole index and filtered, so the cost still grew with every recorded pull request, which is 0062's point. 0004's unique pull_requests_repo_branch stays as the table's uniqueness rule.

trickyParts: GitHub does redirect an API call for a transferred repository, which round 1's comments denied: the reviewer measured GET /repos/twitter/bootstrap answering 301 to /repositories/2126244 and GraphQL answering twbs/bootstrap. The half a transfer really moves is the App installation, so the token must follow the pair; addressing the served name is kept because a write should not depend on a redirect and because a log line should name the right repository. Every comment now says that, and the cleanup after the transfer must not rest on the old claim.

The identity mint is a choke point now rather than two call sites: workflowRuntime.identity takes the record's ghrepo.Repository. Both callers already held one and only called .Owner() on it, so each lost code, and a third caller cannot mint on an owner of its own choosing.

NewRenames is where one-owner-to-two-owners is refused, because only it holds every pair; it cannot see which owners the project serves. That makes one earlier ghrepo test case unconstructible — a pair to a served owner beside a pair to an owner outside the project, out of one owner — so that case keeps what it tested with a second `from` owner. Allowing the outside-target shape again would mean moving the rule to a place that knows the project's owners.

pull_requests_lower_repo_branch is not unique. Making it unique is the rule the case-insensitive reads imply — two rows whose repo differs only in case would let PullRequestByBranch pick either — but it changes what the table accepts and could fail on existing rows, so it is not done here; 0004's unique pull_requests_repo_branch stays as the table's uniqueness rule, unchanged from main.
deviations: Round 2 finding 1 offered a stronger shape for the READY mint as well (one helper, built on implementClient, as the only way to get an implement client for a recorded repository). It was taken for the identity, where both callers collapse onto one function; it was not taken for the API, where readyNote mints a lease through leaseForGrant rather than building a client, and where server.serving is already the one rule the two API sites read.

Round 2 finding 4's wording said the reads scan the table; measured on PostgreSQL 18 they walked the whole index and filtered. The fix stands and the comment states the measurement rather than the wording.
